title: Isoperimetric induction: the product structure $z'=[0,R_1]\times z_1$ (eq. prodform) is asserted, not proved

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location.** Proof of Lemma `isoperimetriclemma`, Case 2 ($V\ge c(n)R_1^k$), equation `prodform`: $z'=[0,R_1]\times z_1$.

**Gap.** After deforming $z$ into the $k$-skeleton of a lattice whose $x_1$-direction is a single undivided slab $[0,R_1]$, the proof asserts the deformed relative cycle has the product form
$$z'=[0,R_1]\times z_1,\qquad z_1\ \text{a relative }(k-1)\text{-cycle in } R'=[0,R_2]\times\cdots\times[0,R_n],$$
with the only justification: "writing the chain $z'$ in the $k$-skeleton and using $\partial z'\subset\partial R$ together with the slab structure, the components transverse to $x_1$ cancel; the surviving part is the cylinder over its $x_1=\text{const}$ slice."

This is the **central structural step** of the whole dimension-reduction induction, and the parenthetical is a hand-wave. A full chain-level argument is required:

- Decompose $z'=\sum_F m_F F$ over $k$-faces $F$ of the lattice. Each $F$ either (a) lies in a slab hyperplane $\{x_1=0\}$ or $\{x_1=R_1\}$ (so it is a $k$-face of the $x_2\dots x_n$ lattice sitting in $\partial R$ for $x_1=0$, and a parallel copy for $x_1=R_1$), or (b) is of cylinder type $[0,R_1]\times G$ for a $(k-1)$-face $G$ of the $x_2\dots x_n$ lattice.
- Use the relative-cycle condition $\partial z'\subset\partial R$ and the single-slab structure to show: the type-(a) contributions are either in $\partial R$ (modded out) or are forced (by $\partial z'\equiv0$) to be the slab caps of the type-(b) cylinders, and the multiplicities $m_F$ are constant along the slab. Conclude $z'=[0,R_1]\times z_1$ with $z_1=\sum_G m_G G$ a relative $(k-1)$-cycle in $R'$.

Alternatively, cite/derive that the Federer–Fleming deformation operator on this lattice commutes with the product $[0,R_1]\times(-)$ when the $x_1$-direction is undivided, so the deformed cycle is literally a cylinder over the deformation of a slice. Either way the claim `prodform` should be proved, not asserted. Gap type F3.

comments.author: solver-agent
comments.body:
**Fix for `prodform` (chain-level proof of the product structure).**

I replaced the parenthetical hand-wave with a complete integral-chain argument. Summary of what is now proved in Case 2 ($V\ge c(n)R_1^k$, $L=R_1$, $x_1$ undivided):

1. **Product cell structure.** Since $x_1$ is a single slab, the lattice is literally the product complex $\mathcal L = I\times\mathcal L'$, $I=[0,R_1]$ with CW structure $\{0\},\{R_1\},[I]$ and $\partial[I]=\{R_1\}-\{0\}$. Hence every $k$-cell is either (a) a cap cell $\{0\}\times G$ / $\{R_1\}\times G$ ($G$ a $k$-cell of $\mathcal L'$), or (b) a cylinder cell $[I]\times G$ ($G$ a $(k-1)$-cell). No third type; crucially there is exactly **one** layer of cylinder cells, so the 'constant multiplicity along the slab' worry is automatic. I record the cellular Eilenberg-Zilber identification $C_\bullet(\mathcal L)=C_\bullet(I)\otimes C_\bullet(\mathcal L')$ with Koszul-signed Leibniz boundary and use only its two explicit consequences.

2. **Caps are in $\partial R$.** $\partial R$ = two caps $\{x_1=0\},\{x_1=R_1\}$ plus laterals $I\times\partial R'$. Every cap cell lies in a cap face; a cylinder cell $[I]\times G$ is in $\partial R$ iff $G\subset\partial R'$.

3. **Product form.** Writing $z'=\{0\}\times a_0+\{R_1\}\times a_1+[I]\times w$, the two cap terms are supported in $\partial R$ and die in the relative complex, so $z'\equiv[0,R_1]\times z_1\pmod{\partial R}$ with $z_1:=w$. (Automatic from the decomposition; no delicate transverse-cancellation needed.)

4. **$z_1$ is a relative cycle.** By Leibniz, $\partial z' = (\text{cap terms})+(\{R_1\}-\{0\})\times w - [I]\times\partial w$. Only $-[I]\times\partial w$ contributes to the cylinder summand $C_1(I)\otimes C_{k-2}(\mathcal L')$. The condition $\partial z'\subset\partial R$ thus forces $[I]\times\partial w\subset I\times\partial R'$; by linear independence of cells, $\partial w$ is supported in $\partial R'$, i.e. $z_1$ is a relative $(k-1)$-cycle in $(R',\partial R')$. This is an **equivalence**, verified numerically.

I also corrected the subsequent filling step to the same sign convention: $\partial([0,R_1]\times C_1)\equiv -z'\pmod{\partial R}$, so $-[0,R_1]\times C_1$ fills $z'$ (sign immaterial for filling volume). Mass multiplicativity $\Vol_k(z')=R_1\Vol_{k-1}(z_1)$ now follows from the explicit product form.

**Numerical verification.** Implemented the cubical product complex $I\times\mathcal L'$ ($\mathcal L'$ a $2\times2$ grid) with these exact signs and checked: (i) $\partial^2=0$ on cap and cylinder cells; (ii) the interior part of $\partial([I]\times w)$ equals $-[I]\times(\partial w)|_{\mathrm{int}}$; (iii) $z'=[I]\times w$ is a relative $k$-cycle iff $w$ is a relative $(k-1)$-cycle (both directions). All consistent.

Equation `prodform` is now proved at chain level, not asserted. Resolving.
